sources.title: Original GLM-5-Turbo launch announcement
sources.evidence: Original Zai_org announcement accessed through X syndication JSON; timestamp 2026-03-15T16:38:58Z. Introduces GLM-5-Turbo as a high-speed GLM-5 variant for agent workflows, with Coding Plan Max, OpenRouter and API access links. Direct X page returned 403; X-owned syndication returned the original account and full text.

sources.title: Developer explanation of closed distribution
sources.evidence: Original Zai_org follow-up, accessed through X syndication, explicitly calls GLM-5-Turbo an experimental closed-source version and says its capabilities/findings will enter a future open-source release. Timestamp 2026-03-15T16:39:01Z.

sources.title: Official model and product release history
sources.evidence: The explicit 2026-03-15 entry announces GLM-5-Turbo for OpenClaw workflows, tools, instructions and extended execution. Date is explicit release text, not a repository or provider-created timestamp.

sources.title: GLM-5-Turbo native API guide
sources.evidence: Full native Markdown documents text input/output, 200K context, 128K maximum output, thinking mode and function calling. States model optimization began during training, including task-data construction and optimization objectives, and compares Turbo separately against GLM-5. Supplies native API examples with thinking enabled/disabled. No model size, active count or architecture topology is disclosed.

sources.title: Exact Z.AI provider route metadata
sources.evidence: Direct JSON identifies the Z.AI route z-ai/glm-5-turbo-20260315 with context_length 202752 and max_completion_tokens 131072. Text modalities, reasoning and tools are listed. These are documented native-provider route limits; no paid inference or live model behavior test was performed.

sources.title: Z.ai API terms and model ownership
sources.evidence: Section V reserves ownership of model parameters, algorithms, code and framework structure; API terms grant limited service-use rights. Supports descriptive proprietary classification for this explicitly closed hosted variant, without importing the MIT license of GLM-5 weights.

sources.title: Official GLM-5 family download table
sources.evidence: Current original repository lists exact 744B-A40B rows for GLM-5, 5.1, 5.2 and 5.3 and 320B-A18B for 5.3-Flash. It has no GLM-5-Turbo weight row or exact Turbo topology/count claim. The table does not establish that Turbo shares another listed checkpoint.

sources.title: GLM-5 technical report
sources.evidence: Checked the full report and architecture/count tables. Their MoE, MLA/DSA and 744B/40B statements identify GLM-5, not GLM-5-Turbo; Turbo is not named. These predecessor specifications are not transferred.

name.note: Exact released name; distinct from GLM-5V-Turbo.

developer.note: Original developer announcement and native API documentation.

family.note: Developer explicitly identifies this as a GLM-5 variant within GLM.

release_date.note: Explicit native release-history date agrees with original public launch at 16:38:58 UTC on March 15. This is March 16 in Beijing and explains a possible day-label difference; use earliest evidenced UTC public availability.

open_weights.note: Developer explicitly announced a closed-source experimental model. Current original download table supplies no Turbo checkpoint; no subsequent open-weight release was found in the checked exact-model sources.

license.note: Descriptive classification for closed hosted distribution governed by API terms; GLM-5 MIT weights are a separate release.

parameters_b.note: No total count for this exact variant in accessed native documentation, original download table, later model cards or reports. 744B reported for GLM-5 cannot establish Turbo size.

active_parameters_b.note: No exact Turbo active-parameter count is disclosed in checked original sources. Do not copy GLM-5 40B based on branding or the high-speed variant label.

architecture.note: Native documentation establishes training optimization and a model variant, but does not specify dense/MoE topology or attention design. GLM-5 MoE/MLA/DSA specifications are not directly assigned to Turbo.

context_window.note: Native guide uses 200K shorthand; exact Z.AI provider-route metadata resolves its served context to 202752. This is a route specification, not an inaccessible checkpoint maximum. The separate output cap is 131072.

modalities.note: Native exact-model guide and route agree on text input and output. External agent tools do not add native image/video input; GLM-5V-Turbo is separate.

reasoning.note: Native API examples explicitly enable or disable thinking and return reasoning content.

tool_call.note: Native guide explicitly supports function calling; exact provider route lists tools and tool_choice.

description.value: Text model trained for OpenClaw workflows, with optional reasoning and tool calling.
description.note: Replaces the vague faster-lane description with directly supported training focus and capabilities. No measured speed or quality claim is added.

patch.description: Text model trained for OpenClaw workflows, with optional reasoning and tool calling.
patch.notes: Released March 15, 2026 UTC (March 16 in Beijing). Z.ai described Turbo as an experimental closed-source variant trained for OpenClaw tasks. Its parameter counts and architecture remain undisclosed in checked original sources; GLM-5 specifications are not inherited. Native docs advertise 200K context; the Z.AI provider route specifies 202752 tokens, with a separate 131072-token output cap.

summary: Reviewed all 14 fields. Corrects release to original March 15 UTC announcement and native served context to 202752, adds proprietary classification and a factual description. Confirms text-only inputs/outputs, thinking and function calling. Total/active counts and topology remain undisclosed after exact-model and later original-source checks. Retained as a distinct trained variant: native documentation describes optimization during training, with no primary same-checkpoint service-tier mapping.
